overall: The AG found the Fall River School Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any of the five allegations raised across four complaints by a single complainant.

allegations.summary: Complainant said the March 12 meeting was not open because the meeting room was hard to find, despite the notice listing the building.
allegations.key_passage: However, here, the meeting notice clearly stated the meeting room.

allegations.summary: Complainant said he was not allowed to speak during the March 12 public comment period because he was not on the sign-up sheet.
allegations.key_passage: We find no error in how the Committee handled public comment during the March 12 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant said a photo the mayor allegedly took of him during the meeting should have been listed as a document or exhibit used at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that any photo that may or may not have been taken was not used during the March 12 meeting and did not need to be listed in the meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant said the committee violated the law by discussing his complaint in executive session without inviting him.
allegations.key_passage: The body, therefore, has no obligation under the Open Meeting Law to include a complainant in the executive session discussion of an Open Meeting Law complaint.

allegations.summary: Complainant said the committee discussed a staff member in executive session without listing that person on the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee did not discuss any topics during the April 9 executive session other than those listed on the meeting notice, and we therefore find no violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the April 9 executive session notice misstated the nature of the complaints being reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: we note that this would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, even if true.
